cards.ex: Come on in! Make yourself at home.
Don't peek at the answers! → He scribbled his number on a napkin. (peek at N, scribble down N)
What can I get you? — Same as usual, please.
The kids gobbled up the pizza. → I cuddled my dog on the sofa. (gobble up N, cuddle with N)
Your phone was in the car? What a relief!

quiz.q: Come in and sit down. Make yourself at ___ .
quiz.note: Make yourself at home = 편하게 계세요. 손님 맞을 때 단골 표현.

quiz.q: No ___ ! I want it to be a surprise.
quiz.note: peek = 몰래 살짝 보다. No peeking! = 훔쳐보기 없기!
Same as usual = 늘 그렇지. 카페에서 '늘 먹던 걸로'라고 할 때도.

quiz.q: The dog ___ his food in ten seconds.
The test was canceled? What a ___ !
quiz.note: What a relief! = 휴, 다행이다! relief는 명사, relieved는 형용사 (I'm relieved).

cards.ko: 악감정 없어요, 기분 나쁘게 생각 마
cards.ex: I picked Jake for the team. No hard feelings? — Of course not.
Stop dawdling, we're late! → No loitering in front of the store. (dawdle over N, No loitering = 배회 금지)
I finally started learning to swim at 40. Better late than never!

cards.ko: (약속을) 펑크 내다 / 사소한 걸 트집 잡다
cards.ex: He flaked on me again. → Stop nitpicking my essay. (flake on 사람, flaky = 약속 잘 깨는)
Thanks for the flowers. You made my day!

quiz.q: Sorry I said no to your idea. No hard ___ ?
quiz.note: No hard feelings = 악감정 없지? / 기분 나쁘게 생각 마. 항상 복수 feelings.

quiz.q: Teenagers were ___ outside the mall all night.
quiz.note: loiter = 할 일 없이 한곳에 서성이다. No loitering 표지판 자주 봐요.

quiz.q: You came to my party two hours late? Well, better late ___ never.
quiz.note: Better late than never = 늦어도 안 하는 것보단 낫다. than (then X).

quiz.q: She said she'd come, but she ___ on me at the last minute.
quiz.note: flake on 사람 = 약속을 펑크 내다. 그런 사람은 flaky.

quiz.q: Your message really ___ my day. Thank you!
quiz.note: make someone's day = 누군가를 아주 기쁘게 하다.

cards.ex: You've been late three times this week. You're on thin ice.

cards.ko: 우쭐대는, 잘난 척하는 / 콧대 높은, 거만한
cards.ex: A smug smile → a snooty waiter (smug = 자기만족에 빠진, snooty = 남을 깔보는)

cards.expr: Let the cat out of the bag
cards.ex: Don't let the cat out of the bag. The party is a surprise!
Giddy with excitement → a sulky teenager (giddy = 들떠서 어쩔 줄 모르는, sulk = 삐치다)
My brother and I don't always see eye to eye on politics.

quiz.q: After breaking the vase, the kid knew he was on ___ .
quiz.note: be on thin ice = 살얼음판을 걷다. 한 번만 더 잘못하면 끝.

quiz.q: He gave me a ___ look after winning the argument.
quiz.note: smug = 자기가 잘났다고 우쭐하는. a smug look/grin.

quiz.q: Who ___ ? Now she knows about the surprise party!
accept: let the cat out of the bag
quiz.note: let the cat out of the bag = 비밀을 누설하다. let의 과거도 let.

quiz.q: She's been ___ all day because she didn't get the role.
quiz.note: sulky = 삐쳐서 말 안 하는. 동사 sulk (She's sulking).

quiz.q: The director and the writer don't ___ about the ending.
quiz.note: see eye to eye (on/about N) = 의견이 같다. 주로 부정문.
